newsitem.title: USA: BARSHEFSKY-JAPAN SHOULD NOT EXPORT WAY OUT OF WOES.
newsitem.headline: BARSHEFSKY-JAPAN SHOULD NOT EXPORT WAY OUT OF WOES.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky repeated Wednesday that Japan should not rely too much on exports to improve its economy and expressed disappointment in a recent drop in U.S. automotive sector sales to Japan.
"Obviously we are concerned that Japan not export its way out of its current economic situation," Barshefsky told reporters at a briefing.

In 1995, the United States and Japan reached a trade agreement which called on Tokyo to deregulate its automotive parts market to give foreign suppliers more access and to encourage more dealers to sell American brand cars.

However, since the agreement the U.S. trade deficit with Japan has deteriorated rather than improve. The automotive sector now accounts for 66 percent of the U.S. deficit with Japan compared to 60 percent two years ago.
The United States will hold consultations with Japan on automotive issues this fall and will release a report on the status of the pact after those discussions, Barshefsky said.
